lina (acme): Hi, we've started getting consistent 400s from the runtime for fn calls after upgrading the SDK. Error: "function args do not match schema: missing required key 'session_id'". RequestID: req_8a7f9c. Happens on ~10% of calls, higher latency too (~1.8s).

sophie (support): Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste a minimal request payload and the exact SDK version? Also does the error body include the original payload?

lina (acme): SDK 2.1.3. Here's the exact body we send (redacted):
```json
{
  "model": "gpt-4o-mini",
  "function": "createOrder",
  "args": {
    "order": {"items": [123, 456], "total": 42.5},
    "metadata": {}
  }
}
```
The runtime error shows schema expecting metadata.session_id and metadata.client_time. If we set metadata.session_id it works. But customers hit this when our front-end submits an empty metadata object.

alex (eng): Thanks — this looks like JSON-mode schema strictness combined with the fncall validation path. If metadata is an empty object the runtime validates against the declared function schema (metadata.session_id required) and rejects. Two quick clarifications: are you using JSON-mode (i.e., structured output / function calling) and are headers set to application/json?

lina (acme): Yes JSON-mode. Content-Type: application/json. We only see this on a subset of flows where the browser omits metadata entirely and our client library populates metadata as {} before sending.

marcus (solutions): Short-term mitigation: set metadata to null instead of {} when empty, or include a default session_id at the client level. Long-term: runtime should accept absent keys if the schema marks them optional OR coerce empty-object -> null for nested optional objects.

sophie (support): I'm escalating to eng-oncall with request id and repro. Also noting customer is concerned about billing since these failed calls still consumed tokens. @alex can you confirm whether failed fncall validation is billed?

ops-bot: Incident: fncall-schema-400 spike detected (10m window). Link to runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/fncall-schema-400

alex (eng): Quick answers: validation failures are currently charged for the input tokens (we bill on request acceptance), so yes they can show up in usage. Root cause: the function descriptor for createOrder declares metadata.session_id as required. Reproducer: run this curl to hit the same path: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/infer -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-mini","function":"createOrder","args":{"order":{"items":[123],"total":10},"metadata":{}}}'
```
I'll push a short-term runtime patch to relax validation for empty nested objects (coerce {} -> null) in the fncall path; ETA ~2h. We'll also add a lint in the SDK to avoid serializing empty metadata objects.

marcus (solutions): Please add a note for the support playbook: advise customers to send null or include minimal session_id. We'll also surface a billing credit if usage spike > X due to this bug.

sophie (support): Thanks — I'm sending the customer the curl workaround and ETA. Will update once patch is live. :thumbsup:

lina (acme): Thanks, appreciate the fast turnaround — will patch our client as well.

alex (eng): Patch deployed to canary; monitoring for error rate and latency. Will follow up when fully rolled out.
